svg.title: $515,000 Earned Fees to $231,750 Owner Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-fee-profit-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: $515,000 Earned Fees to $231,750 Owner Profit; subtitle: Six bars reconcile the Formula v2.0 Base-Case 45.0% net margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: The first bar is gross operator fee revenue, the next four are negative expense movements, and the final bar is an absolute ending total rather than an additional movement. All figures are annual USD. The operator earns its own contracted fees; client recovery principal is excluded rather than grossed up and reduced by a retained-share factor. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment still applies to third-party consideration. Owner profit is after the modeled business expenses, before owner personal taxes, with no extra owner salary deducted. Contractor fees plus evidence costs are variable delivery costs; technology plus overhead are recurring operating costs.; caption: $515,000 − $174,000 − $36,000 − $28,500 − $44,750 = $231,750; $231,750 ÷ $515,000 = 45.0%.; stages: label: Earned operator fees; value: $515,000 annual fee revenue; numeric value: 515000.0; detail: The illustrative lane mix contributes $300,000 from drawback, $150,000 from tariff refunds, and $65,000 from settlement distributions. Approximately $1.717 million in client recoveries supports these fees at 30%; that recovery principal is excluded.; label: Contractor delivery expense; value: −$174,000 annual specialist expense; numeric value: -174000.0; detail: Budget the three core contractors collectively: licensed broker, evidence analyst, and trade or settlement counsel. Their compensation is an operator expense, not a second claim against the client's recovered principal.; label: Evidence acquisition expense; value: −$36,000 annual case expense; numeric value: -36000.0; detail: Budget purchased records, scanning, retrieval, and secure document delivery separately from contractor labor. Paid accounts consume $24,600 under lane budgets; another $11,400 covers screened, unresolved, and unsuccessful account evidence.; label: Technology and subscriptions; value: −$28,500 annual platform expense; numeric value: -28500.0; detail: Cover manifest intelligence, authorized record reconciliation, secure storage, accounting, and document workflow software. Do not assume public manifests replace private entry evidence or provide unrestricted ACE account access.; label: Insurance and operating overhead; value: −$44,750 annual overhead expense; numeric value: -44750.0; detail: Cover insurance, accounting, prospecting, routine administration, and modest bond-related expense where contracted. Together with technology, recurring costs total $73,250 annually, or $6,104.17 monthly, inside the $1,500–$9,500 planning range.; label: Owner operating profit; value: $231,750 ending total; 45.0% margin; numeric value: 231750.0; detail: Total annual expenses equal $283,250. Conservative economics remain $110,000 revenue, $74,800 expenses, and $35,200 profit at 32%; scaled economics remain $920,000 revenue, $386,400 expenses, and $533,600 profit at 58%.

circle.title: label: Earned operator fees; value: $515,000 annual fee revenue; numeric value: 515000.0; detail: The illustrative lane mix contributes $300,000 from drawback, $150,000 from tariff refunds, and $65,000 from settlement distributions. Approximately $1.717 million in client recoveries supports these fees at 30%; that recovery principal is excluded.

label: Contractor delivery expense; value: −$174,000 annual specialist expense; numeric value: -174000.0; detail: Budget the three core contractors collectively: licensed broker, evidence analyst, and trade or settlement counsel. Their compensation is an operator expense, not a second claim against the client's recovered principal.

label: Evidence acquisition expense; value: −$36,000 annual case expense; numeric value: -36000.0; detail: Budget purchased records, scanning, retrieval, and secure document delivery separately from contractor labor. Paid accounts consume $24,600 under lane budgets; another $11,400 covers screened, unresolved, and unsuccessful account evidence.

label: Technology and subscriptions; value: −$28,500 annual platform expense; numeric value: -28500.0; detail: Cover manifest intelligence, authorized record reconciliation, secure storage, accounting, and document workflow software. Do not assume public manifests replace private entry evidence or provide unrestricted ACE account access.

label: Insurance and operating overhead; value: −$44,750 annual overhead expense; numeric value: -44750.0; detail: Cover insurance, accounting, prospecting, routine administration, and modest bond-related expense where contracted. Together with technology, recurring costs total $73,250 annually, or $6,104.17 monthly, inside the $1,500–$9,500 planning range.

label: Owner operating profit; value: $231,750 ending total; 45.0% margin; numeric value: 231750.0; detail: Total annual expenses equal $283,250. Conservative economics remain $110,000 revenue, $74,800 expenses, and $35,200 profit at 32%; scaled economics remain $920,000 revenue, $386,400 expenses, and $533,600 profit at 58%.

text.title: Assumptions: The first bar is gross operator fee revenue, the next four are negative expense movements, and the final bar is an absolute ending total rather than an additional movement. All figures are annual USD. The operator earns its own contracted fees; client recovery principal is excluded rather than grossed up and reduced by a retained-share factor. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment still applies to third-party consideration. Owner profit is after the modeled business expenses, before owner personal taxes, with no extra owner salary deducted. Contractor fees plus evidence costs are variable delivery costs; technology plus overhead are recurring operating costs.
